text.tspan: FSx for Lustre deployment options: Scratch vs Persistent
• Data is NOT replicated: if a file server fails,
• High burst: up to 6x the 200 MB/s per TiB baseline
• No backups · cheapest · Use: optimise costs
• Long-term storage and processing, sensitive data
• SSD/HDD: data replicated within the SAME AZ
• Failed file server replaced within minutes
• Daily backups to S3 · Persistent 2 = latest gen
• Link a bucket with a data repository association: objects appear as files; content is loaded from S3 the first time you open the file.
• Write the output of computations back to S3 (automatic export or export tasks).
• Throughput per TiB (docs): Scratch 200 · Persistent 2 SSD 125/250/500/1000 · Persistent 1 SSD 50/100/200 · Persistent 1 HDD 12/40 MB/s.
• Exam: "temporary, cheapest, short job" → Scratch · "long-running, must survive a server failure" → Persistent.
